planting.note: Set divisions or nursery starts in spring or fall into well-drained, humus-rich soil at the edge of woodland or in dappled shade; mulch lightly the first season while roots establish.

directions: This is a rare mint-family perennial native to limestone forests and rocky ledges of the Cumberland Plateau in Alabama and Tennessee, where it is considered endangered in the wild. Upright, often red-tinged stems carry opposite, lance-shaped leaves that release a light fragrance when crushed, topped in late spring to early summer by whorled, stacked clusters of soft white to pale pink flowers with faint purple spotting. It performs best in part sun with average, well-drained soil and is noted as both drought-tolerant once established and deer-resistant. North Creek Nurseries lists it as a new introduction for 2026, suited to woodland gardens and naturalized meadow edges.
sources: North Creek Nurseries (northcreeknurseries.com) — New Introductions for 2026

planting.note: Plant divisions or nursery starts in spring or fall in part shade to full shade; tolerates full sun only if soil is kept consistently moist.

directions: 'Pleasant Stream' is a 2026 North Creek Nurseries introduction selected for its glossy, deep-green foliage, which is noticeably smoother than the fuzzy leaves typical of the species. Bright pink, daisy-like flowers open in early spring on short stems above the basal rosette, drawing in early-season pollinators before most other perennials are active. It forms a low, spreading groundcover mat useful for edging paths, filling gaps between stepping stones, or stabilizing shaded slopes, and tolerates dry soil once established in shade though it needs steady moisture if grown in more sun. The plant is deer-resistant and well suited to woodland gardens and naturalized plantings.
sources: North Creek Nurseries (northcreeknurseries.com) — New Introductions for 2026

scientific_name: Scutellaria 'Bumblebee Blues' (S. ovata x S. serrata)

planting.note: Plant divisions or nursery starts in spring in full sun to part sun and average, well-drained soil; established clumps tolerate dry spells.

directions: A 2026 North Creek Nurseries introduction, 'Bumblebee Blues' arose as a sister seedling of 'Appalachian Blues' from a naturally occurring hybrid between Scutellaria ovata and S. serrata found in the mountains of West Virginia, selected by plantsman Peter Heus. Deep purple stems and serrated foliage set off large clusters of hooded, salvia-like, rich cobalt-blue flowers with white throats from late spring into summer. Compared with its sister selection it grows taller and produces more flowers, forming a sturdy upright clump. It is deer-resistant, drought-tolerant once established, and especially attractive to bumblebees and other pollinators.
sources: North Creek Nurseries (northcreeknurseries.com) — New Introductions for 2026
